title: Speculative & Novel Huffman Decode Approaches
summary: Systematic investigation of approaches to break the serial Huffman dependency chain in DEFLATE decompression. The serial chain (symbol N's bit position depends on symbol N-1's code length) creates a ~6-12 cycle loop-carried dependency per symbol that fundamentally limits single-stream throughput. We evaluated multiple micro-optimization and architectural approaches.

serial_dependency_analysis.description: Each Huffman symbol decode requires: (1) peek bits from buffer, (2) table lookup, (3) extract code length, (4) shift buffer by code length. Steps 1-4 form a sequential chain because step 4 of symbol N determines the bit position for step 1 of symbol N+1.
serial_dependency_analysis.measured_cycle_cost: ~6-12 cycles per symbol on modern x86-64 (table lookup latency + shift)
serial_dependency_analysis.theoretical_max_throughput: At ~8 bits/symbol average and ~8 cycles/symbol at 4 GHz: ~4 GB/s. Our measured ~1.75 GB/s suggests ~60% efficiency.
serial_dependency_analysis.implication: Single-stream throughput is bounded by this chain. Wider tables or faster bit manipulation cannot eliminate it — only reduce the constant factor.

experiments_conducted.name: Branchless length-extra extraction
experiments_conducted.description: Always extract extra bits for length/distance codes, mask to 0 when extra_bits=0, avoiding the conditional branch.
experiments_conducted.result: No sustained improvement under 50-iteration benchmarks. The compiler already handles the conditional efficiently via cmov or branch prediction.
experiments_conducted.conclusion: The branch predictor handles this pattern well; removing it doesn't help.

experiments_conducted.name: Single-refill strategy for backrefs
experiments_conducted.description: Perform one large refill at the start of the backref path instead of per-field refill checks for length, distance, and extra bits.
experiments_conducted.result: Marginal-to-no improvement. The bit reader already has 56+ bits after refill, enough for most complete litlen+dist+extras sequences.
experiments_conducted.conclusion: The existing refill strategy is already near-optimal.

experiments_conducted.name: 4-literal unrolled loop
experiments_conducted.description: Unroll the main decode loop to attempt 4 consecutive literal decodes before checking for non-literal symbols.
experiments_conducted.result: Performance regression. The complex control flow (fallback from any position in the 4-literal sequence to backref handling) confused the compiler's optimization and branch prediction.
experiments_conducted.conclusion: The current 3-literal cascade (attempt 1, try 2nd, try 3rd) is the sweet spot.

experiments_conducted.name: Inline short-copy for common matches
experiments_conducted.description: For matches <= 8 bytes with distance >= 8, inline the copy directly in the decode loop instead of calling fast_copy().
experiments_conducted.result: Performance regression. The additional branch to check match length hurt more than the avoided function call overhead.
experiments_conducted.conclusion: fast_copy() with __builtin_expect is already well-optimized by the compiler.

novel_approaches_evaluated.name: Multi-stream ILP (interleaved sub-streams)
novel_approaches_evaluated.description: Decode 2-4 independent Huffman streams in parallel within a single thread, interleaving instructions to hide latency.
novel_approaches_evaluated.feasibility: NOT FEASIBLE for standard DEFLATE. The format specifies a single bitstream per block. Would require a custom compression format (like GDeflate or Brotli's multi-stream).
novel_approaches_evaluated.conclusion: Cannot be applied to standard ZIP files without format modification.

novel_approaches_evaluated.name: Speculative decode with rollback
novel_approaches_evaluated.description: Speculatively decode symbol N+1 assuming the most common code length for symbol N, then verify and rollback if wrong.
novel_approaches_evaluated.feasibility: MARGINAL. The verification cost (~3 cycles for compare+branch) plus rollback cost (~5-10 cycles to restore state) means net benefit only if prediction accuracy > 80%. For typical Huffman distributions, the most common code length covers 40-60% of symbols.
novel_approaches_evaluated.conclusion: Risk/reward ratio is poor. Implementation complexity is high, and mispredict penalty erases gains. The 3-literal cascade already achieves a similar effect for the literal-only case.

novel_approaches_evaluated.name: Convergence-based parallel sync
novel_approaches_evaluated.description: Start decoding from multiple points in the bitstream simultaneously, using the fact that incorrect starting positions will eventually produce invalid Huffman codes, allowing detection and correction.
novel_approaches_evaluated.feasibility: THEORETICALLY INTERESTING but impractical. Convergence distance is unpredictable (could be 1 symbol or 1000+). The correction overhead dominates for typical block sizes.
novel_approaches_evaluated.conclusion: Better suited for very large blocks (>1MB). Our corpus blocks average 64-262KB.

novel_approaches_evaluated.name: Precomputed mega-table (16+ bit lookup)
novel_approaches_evaluated.description: Use a very wide primary table (14-16 bits) to decode 2-3 symbols per lookup more frequently.
novel_approaches_evaluated.feasibility: FEASIBLE but diminishing returns. 14-bit table = 64KB (fits L1). 16-bit table = 256KB (blows L1). Our 11-bit + secondary table already handles >99% of codes in primary lookup.
novel_approaches_evaluated.conclusion: Marginal gain. The secondary table path is <1% of lookups for typical data. A 12-bit table (8KB) might be worth testing.

novel_approaches_evaluated.name: Parallel block decoding (multi-threaded)
novel_approaches_evaluated.description: Decode multiple DEFLATE blocks on separate threads in parallel.
novel_approaches_evaluated.feasibility: LIMITED. Most real files have 1-5 compressed blocks, each 64-262KB decompressed. The parallelism is severely limited, and inter-block output dependencies (LZ77 can reference previous blocks) make this complex.
novel_approaches_evaluated.theoretical_speedup: Up to Nx for N blocks, but N is typically 1-5
novel_approaches_evaluated.conclusion: Deferred to item_017 for detailed analysis. Go/no-go depends on corpus characteristics.

concept_evolve_probe_results.query: speculative Huffman decoding: breaking serial dependency chain
steering_directions: Convergence-based parallel Huffman with bounded synchronization distance
Neural codeword boundary predictor trained on bitstream statistics
Exploit LZ77 backreference structure for block-level parallelism
Hybrid approach: fixed-length escape codes as synchronization markers
concept_evolve_probe_results.assessment: All 5 directions either require format modification (incompatible with standard ZIP) or have unpredictable convergence properties. The most promising for standard DEFLATE is exploiting LZ77 structure for block-level parallelism (evaluated in item_017).

block_structure_analysis.description: Empirical analysis of DEFLATE block structure across 20-file benchmark corpus at compression levels 1, 6, 9.

findings.typical_block_count: 1-5 blocks for most real data files
findings.stored_blocks: Only appear for incompressible data (random bytes, binary headers)
findings.fixed_huffman: Rarely used (0 out of 20 files at level 6)
findings.dynamic_huffman: Dominant: used by all compressible files

key_conclusions: The serial Huffman dependency chain is the FUNDAMENTAL bottleneck for single-stream DEFLATE decompression.
Micro-optimizations within the existing decode loop architecture yield diminishing returns — we are already at ~60% of the theoretical single-stream limit.

Breaking the 2000 MB/s barrier for backref-heavy data within standard DEFLATE requires either: (a) reducing per-symbol cycle cost below 6 cycles (very hard), or (b) fundamentally different processing model.
The 3-literal cascade (decode up to 3 literals per refill) is the most effective micro-optimization, providing ~4.7x over naive.
SIMD copy, branchless bitreader, and fast table build are important for correctness and edge cases but contribute <5% each to peak throughput on typical data.
Multi-stream and format-modifying approaches (GDeflate, Brotli-style) can achieve 2-4x more but are incompatible with standard ZIP.
Our best remaining optimization vectors are: (1) 12-bit primary table, (2) backref fast-path tightening, (3) compiler tuning (PGO/LTO), (4) parallel block decode for multi-block files.

remaining_optimization_vectors.name: 12-bit primary table
remaining_optimization_vectors.description: TESTED: Increased primary table from 11 to 12 bits (4096 entries, 16KB). REGRESSED from ~1750 to ~1574 MB/s. The extra 8KB causes L1 cache pressure that outweighs the subtable lookup savings. 11-bit (8KB) confirmed as optimal, consistent with libdeflate's choice.

remaining_optimization_vectors.name: Tighter backref fast-path
remaining_optimization_vectors.description: Combine length decode, distance decode, and copy into a tighter sequence with fewer branches. Profile-guided optimization of the hot path.

remaining_optimization_vectors.name: Profile-guided optimization (PGO)
remaining_optimization_vectors.description: GCC -fprofile-generate / -fprofile-use on the benchmark corpus. Helps branch prediction and code layout.

remaining_optimization_vectors.name: Link-time optimization (LTO)
remaining_optimization_vectors.description: GCC -flto for whole-program optimization across bitreader.h + fast_decode.c.
